mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 YoY growth < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE > 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which increases input costs and reduces profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,200,000 units signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST falls below 1,200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A positive divergence between payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over three months indicates underreported labor market strength, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > UNRATE decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of positive PAYEMS-UNRATE divergence for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS growth > 5%) signals elevated precautionary behavior, which depresses consumption and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of RSAFS YoY growth > 5%.
